claims.claim: A ~2,000-word article on an Ottoman fortress that never existed passed Articles for Creation by anchoring to a real sultan (Mehmed the Conqueror, 1466), plausible structural detail and well-formatted citations to nonexistent works, surviving from 2023-01 to 2023-12.
claims.source: 404 Media 2024-10 — The Editors Protecting Wikipedia from AI Hoaxes
claims.quote: well-formatted citations referencing completely nonexistent works
claims.page: 404 Media 2024-10 — The Editors Protecting Wikipedia from AI Hoaxes

claims.claim: The 'Leninist historiography' article carried entirely invented references in Russian and Hungarian, where fewer reviewers could check them.
claims.quote: completely fake sources in Russian and Hungarian

claims.claim: AI paragraphs on the beetle Estola albosignata cited real German and French papers that were about unrelated subjects (a crab).
Models cite real sources without checking that the source supports the sentence it is attached to.
claims.quote: will likely not verify the content

claims.claim: LLM-generated encyclopedic text virtually always fails to source its claims properly and often introduces errors.
claims.quote: virtually always fail to properly source claims

claims.claim: A confidently detailed entry can describe a species that does not exist.
LLMs draw conclusions that appear in no single reliable source, i.e. original research delivered in encyclopedic voice.
claims.quote: not present in any single reliable source

claims.claim: Generated text sounds neutral while its substance takes a side, which is hardest to catch in biographies.
claims.quote: neutral-seeming in tone, but not necessarily in substance

claims.claim: Errors arrive plausible-sounding and with an air of confidence, so spot-checking produces false confidence.
claims.quote: plausible-sounding and given with an air of confidence

claims.claim: Faced with an obscure topic the model invents details rather than saying less.
claims.quote: invented details when faced with a prompt on an obscure topic

claims.claim: One subtly false claim or distorted quote embedded in otherwise correct text survives review and misinforms.
claims.quote: one subtly false claim or distorted quote

claims.claim: Generated articles read like advertorials or partisan spin with promotional language mixed into facts.
claims.quote: read like advertorials or partisan spins

claims.feature: fabricated citations in an editor test
claims.claim: In one editor's test five of seven generated citations were fabricated and others led to unrelated articles.
An AI-generated newspaper reading list paired real authors with books that do not exist; patrons then asked librarians to find them.
claims.source: 404 Media 2025 — Librarians Are Being Asked to Find AI-Hallucinated Books
claims.quote: asking him to find books that don't exist
claims.page: 404 Media 2025 — Librarians Are Being Asked to Find AI-Hallucinated Books

claims.claim: ChatGPT biographies were 58.3% atomic-fact precise (InstructGPT 42.5%, search-augmented PerplexityAI 71.5%); all far below humans.
claims.source: Min et al. 2023 — FActScore: Fine-grained Atomic Evaluation of Factual Precision in Long Form Text Generation (arXiv 2305.14251)
claims.page: Min et al. 2023 — FActScore: Fine-grained Atomic Evaluation of Factual Precision in Long Form Text Generation (arXiv 2305.14251)
